correctness.rationale: The proof derives the sharp one-dimensional inequalities and all contact cases explicitly. Any globally optimal product-box function saturates the one-dimensional inequality on every coordinate-axis restriction because the tensor upper bound is valid in every summation order. Vanishing of the two axis Fourier samples and nonnegativity of every joint spectral coefficient force whole hyperplanes of zeros. Complementary Fourier inversion gives a nonsingular two-equation system for each spatial slice; solving it forces factorization along every odd coordinate. Explicit imaginary-phase one-dimensional optimizers prove the even-side nonuniqueness. Direct DFT calculations (81 checks) independently corroborate finite instances; unrestricted correctness rests on the analytic argument, not numerics.

originality.rationale: The precise proposed addition is uniqueness of the complex maximizer for all-odd finite product boxes, together with a sharp even-coordinate failure of uniqueness and forced product Fourier zero mask. The scalar product value, one-dimensional contact inequality, and general Fourier-positivity framework are expressly prior work. Material inspection of the 2003 product theorem and the 2002 small-support cyclic paper, plus actual topic and reduction searches in the publication index and literature, found no theorem whose hypotheses cover this equality-classification claim. This is a best-knowledge conclusion, not a proof of global novelty; older implicit equality cases remain a residual risk.

value.rationale: The precise structural question is whether optimal positive-definite kernels with small Cartesian supports are identifiable or admit non-product extremizers. Although the scalar Turán constant already tensorizes, that fact does not classify its equality face. The result proves a complete all-odd uniqueness theorem, a sharp even-side obstruction, and the exact positive spectral mask for the unique extremizer in every dimension. The parity transition and hyperplane-forced factorization provide a natural full classification of optimizer rigidity for an infinite family of boxes, not a routine numerical improvement.
